name: wait_ticks
description:
Hold the current command and let simulated time pass.
Use when: the scene has to change without a robot command -- a released object is still settling, or the task says to wait. It is not a correction: a pose residual needs move_pose, a stalled jaw needs set_gripper.
Effect: world mutation by elapsed time only. Each tick resends the arm's held joint targets, with zero base velocity, and leaves the gripper directive as it is; nothing is planned, the joint controller holds the arm where its last motion left it, and any drift is measured. ticks control ticks elapse, one tick being one RoboCasa control step (50 ms of simulated time, 20 Hz), at most 20 per call. One call is one robot decision.
Returns: status=submitted immediately. The next receipt reports wait.ticks_used, wait.physics_steps and the arm's inactive_arm_drift while held; the fresh observation shows what changed.
Does not: move toward any target, open or close the gripper, restore a drifted pose, or establish that the scene changed.
On error: Refused: any field other than ticks, or ticks that is not an integer from 1 to 20 (invalid_arguments, naming the ticks bound); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). For more time call wait_ticks again; act once a fresh observation shows the scene you need. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: last_action_effect.detail.wait.claim_boundary is "time passed with commands held; drift, settling, slip or scripted scene motion are measured evidence in the fresh observation, not effects of this action".

ticks.description: Control ticks to hold the current command. One tick is one RoboCasa control step (50 ms of simulated time); 20 ticks is 1.0 s. Required.
